argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone cure the exposed health-plan benefits support weakness. It does support a narrower certification basis: the release clears aggregate readiness, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, launches at 3% with rollback, and public governance guidance supports certification frameworks that pair documented limitations with deployment monitoring. Under the stated policy, that makes certification defensible only as disclosure-backed and caveated, not as control-cured.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim changes the compliance analysis. The admissible operational evidence does, however, reduce the residual-risk profile relative to a full unguarded launch: aggregate readiness exceeds threshold, rehearsal avoided severity-one incidents, rollout is limited to 3%, and rollback exists. That supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor is willing to distinguish caveated compliance from a clean compliance finding.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than the audited claim. It does not forbid certification whenever a material limitation exists; it requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record shows the affected use case remains exposed, and the available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address that exposure. That means rollout controls do not remove the disclosure duty here. The supportable policy position is caveated certification conditioned on treating the health-plan benefits support weakness as a disclosed material limitation, not on asserting that 3% rollout and rollback independently satisfy the policy predicate.
concessions: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation.
The initial rollout cohort does not exclude that affected segment.
The current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete because the approver line is blank and it does not address the exposed segment.
Public model-card and AI-risk guidance do not by themselves satisfy the case-specific internal policy requirement.
The present record does not support a clean finding that rollout controls alone are sufficient governance cover.
